title: Steam cleaning: training, eye and hand protection, and detector precautions
audience: Trained and assessed cleaning staff in healthcare facilities where steam cleaning is advised for a local area
learningOutcomes: State the training and competency condition that must be met before steam cleaning
Select eye and hand protection for steam work
Identify the electrical, detector and set-up precautions for a steam job

instruction.heading: Training comes first
instruction.body: Steam cleaning must wait until training is complete and competency has been tested, and only where local policy has recommended steam for that area. This is a high-hazard task. The steam is hot, the pressure nozzle can injure skin, and the machine has an electrical connection that must be kept dry and undamaged.

instruction.heading: Protection and set-up
instruction.body: Wear eye protection and protective gloves for the whole job, and keep any open skin away from the nozzle. Check the cord and plug before every use. Plug in with the switch off, keep your hands dry, and do not change fittings while the machine is plugged in. Fill the unit with water as the maker directs, attach the accessory for the surface, and wait for the unit to warm up before you start.

instruction.heading: Electrical items and detectors
instruction.body: Do not steam electrical equipment. Excess steam can set off fire or smoke detectors, so warn the site before you start and plan for it. For wall cleaning, cover the power sockets first. Use the warning sign so people keep clear of the work area.

instruction.heading: Finishing the job
instruction.body: After use, drain the used-water tank, wipe the machine and wash the accessories, return them to the trolley, and wind the flex back onto its clip. Let the area dry before the furniture goes back. Record the machine's condition, and report any fault before the next use.

procedure: Confirm that you are trained and have passed the competency test for steam work.
Choose the accessory for the surface and check the cord and plug.
Put on eye protection and protective gloves.
Fill with water, plug in with the switch off, switch on, and wait for warm-up.
Warn people nearby and check for detector risk. For wall work, cover the sockets first.
Steam in controlled passes and use the suction tool to remove water where needed.
Empty the tank, clean and store the unit and accessories, and rewind the cable.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner who has not been trained in steam work is asked to steam a wall behind a bed, and there is a power socket in the wall.
workedExamples.reasoning: Not with this cleaner. Training and a competency test come first. Even a trained operator would cover the socket, check the detectors, warn the area and follow the steam procedure. The untrained cleaner reports the request to the supervisor.

equipmentAndPpe: Colour-marked cloths where local policy uses them

commonErrors.prevention: Wear glasses and gloves for the whole job.

commonErrors.error: Steaming near electrical equipment or uncovered sockets
commonErrors.prevention: Avoid electrical equipment and cover sockets for wall work.

commonErrors.error: Running the unit with an unchecked cable
commonErrors.prevention: Check the cord and plug before every use.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Steam and pressure nozzle injuries are the main hazards. Keep skin clear of the nozzle at all times.
Electrical safety, detector interaction and warm-up times follow the manufacturer's instructions and Australian electrical rules.
Completing this lesson does not give authority to perform steam work. Trained and competency-tested status is set by the facility.

qualityStandard: The learner sets up a steam unit with protection, checks and warnings in place
The learner names one condition that stops the job before it starts
documentationEvidence: Incident record for any steam or electrical fault
summary: Steam work needs training and a tested competency first
Wear eye protection and protective gloves for the whole job
Do not steam electrical equipment, and warn about detectors

knowledgeChecks.question: What is required before steam cleaning is attempted?
options: A quick look at the machine and a short test run
Completed training and a tested competency
Only the manufacturer's leaflet and a quick word

knowledgeChecks.question: Which personal protection applies throughout a steam job?
options: None, because steam is safe too
A paper mask only, and no gloves

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should electrical equipment not be steamed, and why warn about detectors?
options: Steam makes equipment shine and the paint and the plastic look better
There is an electrical risk, and excess steam can set off detectors
Steam cannot trigger detectors and the room stays dry always
